gpt.text:
Run the three “Next Commands” in order; they’re set up to (1) search module variants and pick the best, (2) run system-level candidates, then (3) generate a suggested fix plan based on results.

## 1) Module-level autopilot (AUB) + select best
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --run --select-best
```
What it does:
- Executes the module experiment suite defined in `module_registry.yaml`.
- Scores candidates against your current champion (`baseline/champion_v5_latest.json`).
- If any candidate beats the champion, it should promote/select it (depending on your tool’s semantics) and record the outcome in the run artifacts.

Quick checks after:
- Look for a “best candidate” summary in the output logs.
- Confirm whether a new champion file was written/updated (often under `baseline/` or a `runs/` directory).

## 2) System-level autopilot (end-to-end)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py \
  --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml \
  --run
```
What it does:
- Runs end-to-end/system candidates defined in `system_candidates.yaml`.
- Produces system-level metrics and comparisons (this is usually where regressions show up even if module-level looks good).

Quick checks after:
- Ensure system metrics are emitted and comparable (same eval set/seed as usual).
- Note any candidates marked PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE.

## 3) Generate “next fix” report (actionable plan)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
What it does:
- Reads the current experiment state/results and proposes the next most promising fix or investigation steps.
- Writes a markdown report to `baseline/reports/next_fix.md`.

## If you want a tight loop / sanity checklist
- Verify you’re on the intended commit/branch and have the expected Python env activated.
- Confirm the champion file exists: `baseline/champion_v5_latest.json`.
- After step (1), re-check the “Current Champion” metrics printed by your tooling to see if they changed.
- After step (2), ensure no candidate improves module metrics but degrades system metrics (common mismatch).

If you paste the stdout (or the produced report paths) from command (1), I can help interpret whether a new champion was selected and what to run next.
